text:
Mitchell Chaffee scored on Nov. 5 against Carolina, a tip in front, and it was his first NHL goal since the 2024-25 season. For an undrafted 28-year-old who has bounced between Minnesota, Tampa Bay and now the Islanders, that kind of night matters. NHL.com also featured him that week talking about his appreciation for his wife's military service.

His role is small. He's playing under 10 minutes a night in eight games, with 14 hits, and he's there because the Islanders are missing three regular forwards. The Islanders have been outchanced when he's out there, about 10 points of expected goal share worse than without him, which is common for fourth-line call-ups.

Evolving-Hockey had too little of him last season to say much, 105 minutes, and his track record before that is mostly AHL and college (he had his best college season at UMass). Our range says 5 to 14 goals over a full season, which assumes a role he probably won't have. When Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie come back, his minutes are the ones that go. Until then, he gets a chance to stick.
headline: Chaffee's chance to stick
